title: Why Jesus Asked “Do You Love Me?” Three Times — John 21:17
paragraphs: Why Jesus Asked “Do You Love Me?” Three Times — John 21:17

He didn’t ask once.
He didn’t ask twice.
He asked three times.
“Do you love Me?” — Gospel of John 21:17

That’s not small talk.
That’s surgery.

Because days earlier, Peter didn’t just stumble—he collapsed under pressure.
Three times he denied Jesus.
Three times he said, “I don’t know Him.”
Now Jesus meets him on the shore… not with anger, not with a lecture—but with a question that cuts deeper than shame.
“Do you love Me?”
Again.
“Do you love Me?”
Again.
“Do you love Me?”
Why three?

Because Jesus wasn’t trying to shame Peter.
He was restoring him at the level he broke.

Every denial… met with an invitation.
Every failure… answered with grace.
But here’s what we miss—

Jesus didn’t say, “Explain yourself.”
He didn’t say, “Prove your loyalty.”
He didn’t even say, “Apologize better.”

He said:
“Do you love Me?”

Because love is the root.
If love is real, everything else can be rebuilt.
And notice this—each time Peter says yes, Jesus responds:
“Feed My sheep.”

Translation?
Your failure did not cancel your calling.
Let that hit.

The man who publicly denied Christ
became the man who would publicly preach Christ.

Not because he was strong—
but because Jesus is merciful.

Some scholars interpret the shift in Greek words for “love” (agape and phileo) as significant—showing Jesus meeting Peter in his brokenness. Others see it as stylistic repetition. But either way, the message stands unshaken:
Jesus meets you where you failed… and calls you forward anyway.

So if you’ve denied Him—
with your words, your silence, your lifestyle—
This question is for you too:
“Do you love Me?”

Not to condemn you.
To call you back.

Because the cross already settled your sin.
And the resurrection secured your restoration.

Come back.
Answer Him honestly.
And let grace rebuild what shame tried to bury.
